# 和漢三才図会 — 唐柿 = 無花果 (THE FIG), not the tomato
# NDL pid 2569764 (文政7/1824 printing) and pid 2596415 (Edo-period printing)
# Text quoted from the NDL full-text (OCR) index, 2026-08-31. NO SCAN IS HELD.

いちじゆく たうかき 無花果 映日果 … 俗云 丁熟 又云 唐柿

按 無花果 其實似柹 而本邦俗曰 唐柿 一月而熟 故名

"The fig (ichijiku), whose fruit resembles a persimmon; in our country it is
commonly called TOGAKI, because it ripens in one month, hence the name."

THE POINT: 唐柿 in Japanese most commonly denotes FICUS CARICA, the fig, NOT the
tomato. Attested in two independent printings of the standard Japanese illustrated
encyclopedia. See the false_friends/japanese_togaki entry in docs/thesaurus.yaml.
